# ItemEditing's component arms type before the editor's text is selected

## Context

Vega's defect note (19 Nov, 17:33Z): `test/playwright/component/list/ItemEditing.spec.mjs:147`, "AC-4: a tree renames a leaf and a folder", failed on #21491's components run `44576392493`. That PR's diff has no list file. The rendered name read `a.txtnotes.txt` where the arm expects `notes.txt`. The spec is mine, from #21490.

## The Problem

The plugin opens the editor and then sends two messages from the App worker: focus, then select the text. Under CI load, the keys Playwright sends reach the page ahead of the queued selection, so `type('notes.txt')` appends to the old name instead of replacing it. The arms wait for focus or for the value, never for the selection. AC-3 has the same race: its single Backspace empties the field only when the whole text is selected.

Reproduced deterministically by delaying `Neo.main.DomAccess.selectNode` 300 ms in the page. Under that delay `dev`'s spec fails 4 of 7, the four arms that depend on a replaced text, and the AC-4 failure is exactly `a.txtnotes.txt`. A 20× CPU throttle alone does not reproduce it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/list/plugin/ItemEditing.mjs` `startEdit`, the editor's `mounted` handler: `editor.focus(); editor.selectText?.()`.
- `Neo.form.field.Text#selectText` → `Neo.main.DomAccess.selectNode` (`select()` plus `setSelectionRange`).
- `test/playwright/component/list/ItemEditing.spec.mjs`: six arms send their first editing key right after the editor opens.

## The Fix

An `editorReady(page)` helper in the spec polls for the editor input holding the focus with its whole text selected. Each of the six arms awaits it before its first editing key.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: every arm that edits the name waits for the selected text before its first key.
- [ ] AC-2: with `selectNode` delayed 300 ms, the fixed spec passes 7 of 7, where `dev`'s fails 4 of 7.
- [ ] AC-3: the components tier is green on the PR.

## Out of Scope

- Selecting before focusing in the plugin, which would close the same window for a fast typist. That needs a real-browser proof that a programmatic focus keeps an existing selection.
- `WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs:212`, which flaked in the same run and has another owner.
